title: The road less travelled part 4
scripture_text: ’’After this, Jesus travelled about from one town and village to another, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him, and also some women who had been cured of evil spirits and diseases: Mary (called Magdalene from whom seven demons had come out; Joanna the wife of Chuza, the manager of Herod’s household; Susanna; and many others. These women were helping to support them out of their own means.’’
devotional:
To follow Jesus will cause us to turn what we have, into expressions of generosity.

We are told that these women contributed from their own resources. Most people who have written on this passage make the assumption that these must have been wealthy women. We are told that Joanna was the wife of Chuza, Herod’s business manger, so she may have been well off. But I do not think Luke is thinking about the wealth of these women. A better way to read this phrase would be, they used what they had at hand to support Jesus and his disciples. They used what they had, be it much or little.

We have all been designed in such a way that our lives need to be a continual expression of generosity. We have spoken about how difficult it can be to receive. But it can be also difficult to give. In the Hebrew mind and language there is no concept or word for charity. Instead they think in terms of ‘righteousness,’ so for them what we think of as ‘charity,’ they see it as an act of righteousness. This means as followers of Jesus, generosity needs to be a normal expression of who we are. We have a built-in need to be generous. Not only generous with our money, but with our time, our homes, and ourselves. Just let me mention the way the end of verse 3 is written in the Greek, it needs to be understood as a continual action. These women continued to support Jesus.

To follow Jesus means that you intentionally engage in community life.

Joanna who lived a life of relative luxury and power, sharing life with Mary Magdalene whose life had been messed up by seven demons, and Susanna whom we know nothing about, and is only mentioned once in scripture. Joanna, Mary, Susanna, very different women from very different worlds, but they chose to live in community, despite the fact that their lives were so different. They were able to do this because Jesus was at the heart and was the heart of their lives together.

Very sadly we are living in a day where Christians seem to have an antipathy towards community. Consumerism has become the metric by which many people measures a church community, so unless a church meets all their bespoke specific needs they move. Their individualistic understanding of Christianity allows them to wash their hands of any care or responsibility for others.

If you are serious about following Jesus, this road less travelled will require a commitment to care and invest your life in Jesus, by caring and investing your life in others.

A verse of scripture I often think about says. ‘He died for everyone so that those who receive his new life will no longer live for themselves.’ 2 Corinthians 5:15. Jesus died ‘so that we no longer live for ourselves.’

As these women followed Jesus along this less travelled road, ‘every day became a school day.’ As they followed him and invested their lives in him they were continually discovering new things about him. The ordinary stuff of everyday life became holy as Jesus used them as illustrations to teach them about himself and his kingdom.

What an amazing privilege!
prayer: Father, If I am not generous, I have a spiritual problem. Please help me to be generous Lord.
